articles.title_orig: Trump and Putin shake hands as Xi welcomes leaders to summit in China
articles.title_zh: Trump and Putin shake hands as Xi welcomes leaders to summit in China
articles.content_orig:
China's Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russia's Vladimir Putin are pictured together in Shenzhen for the first time - images show the leaders shaking hands
They're in China for the Apec summit. Earlier, Xi welcomed Trump with a hug on the tarmac - a carefully choreographed moment of flattery, writes our correspondent
The pair will have historic trilateral talks with Putin on Thursday - Xi earlier called the Russian leader an "old friend"
Our Russia editor says some newspapers are already calling this visit a "diplomatic victory" for Putin - simply because it's happening
Meanwhile, Trump arrives from the Philippines where he attended another summit - here's a recap of the trip so far
Edited by Manish Pandey, with Laura Bicker, Steve Rosenberg and Stephen McDonell in China and Nada Tawfik travelling with President Trump
Laura Gozzi Europe reporter
Some more now on the interaction between Trump, Putin and Xi.
Russia's Kremlin pool team has posted a video on Telegram showing Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump together on a red carpet ahead of tonight's gala dinner in Shenzhen.
In the video, Trump, Xi and Xi's wife are standing next to each other when Putin approaches.
Trump and Putin - who haven't met since the Russia-US summit in Alaska in August 2025 -  seem to greet each other warmly, shaking hands first and exchanging pats on the shoulder.
It's the first time Xi, Trump and Putin are seen together.
The three leaders are due to meet tomorrow afternoon.
Russian leader Vladimir Putin approached US President Donald Trump ahead of the family photo, and the pair shook hands and exchanged greetings, in front of President Xi.
Nadine Yousif Reporting from Toronto, Canada
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney arrived in China earlier this week
Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has already been in Asia for several days ahead of the Apec summit, where he announced a free trade deal with the Philippines and held a bilateral meeting with China's Xi Jinping.
It's all part of his broader push to reduce Canada's reliance on the US as the country still grapples with Donald Trump's tariffs on its key sectors.
US tariffs have since led Carney to break away from American trade policies vis-a-vis China.
Earlier this year, Canada significantly reduced tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles (EVs), allowing up to 49,000 in the country. The US, meanwhile, still tariffs Chinese EVs at 100%.
Ahead of his meeting with Xi, Carney suggested that China's automotive industry could help replace a gap in Canada's sector if a trade deal with the US is not reached.
Afterwards, China and Canada agreed to further tariff relief on pork and seafood, as well as certain steel and aluminium products.
Neither mentioned vehicles, but Ottawa said Chinese EVs are expected to soon enter the Canadian market.
Closer integration on auto manufacturing with China, however, still depends on where trade talks with the US land.
Negotiations are ongoing and progress has been made but some key differences remain, Carney said this week.
Many in Canada will be watching to see how Carney and Trump interact at Apec.
Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum next to her Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco Alvarez
President Trump is separately meeting with both Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney today in China, the White House says.
All three leaders are attending summit in Shenzhen and they are all members of the Apec group.
Malu Cursino Live reporter
US President Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen for a rare trilateral meeting between him, Vladimir Putin and the host, Xi Jinping.
The red carpet was rolled out as Trump's Air Force One landed in Shenzhen, with President Xi greeting him on the tarmac - what China correspondent Laura Bicker describes as a "carefully choreographed diplomatic moment" .
Quoted by Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua, President Xi has voiced his desire for a "constructive, strategically stable relationship" with Washington.
Several hours before Trump's arrival, Russian leader President Putin landed in Shenzhen, with Putin and Xi holding talks, and the Russian leader saying the foreign policy strategy of the two countries was working.
Trump's Shenzhen arrival follows a 21-hour stay in Manila for the Asean Summit, where he met India's Narendra Modi, Japan's Sanae Takaichi and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
While in the Philippines, Trump signed trade agreements with Thailand and the Philippines - but both are light on details and specific commitments.
At a dinner with South East Asia leaders, the US president said: "This is one of the world's most vibrant and productive regions filled with the tremendous potential."
Filipino President Ferdinand Marcos Jr hosted Trump at the MalacaÃ±ang presidential palace and sent Jollibee fried chicken to the US president's party as a midnight snack.
Trilateral talks between Moscow, Beijing and Washington will be Thursday's focus. Issues relating to global peace will be high on the agenda, according to China's foreign ministry.
A Chinese state-run news agency describes the welcome given to US President Donald Trump as warm, with a salute from the military honour guard, children presenting flowers and fighter jets above.
Xinhua quotes Xi as saying that when he visited the US in September, Trump and his wife made a "special trip to the airport" to welcome them and held a "grand welcoming ceremony".
"I welcome your renewed visit to China and look forward to in-depth exchanges of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global order, and to promote the development of a constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality," the agency quotes Xi as saying.
It adds that Trump thanked Xi for coming to the airport to personally welcome him.
Laura Gozzi Europe reporter
Kremlin senior aide Yury Ushakov has said Putin and Trump - who are due to meet Xi Jinping on Thursday - could meet at tonight's gala dinner.
"And they will definitely meet tomorrow," Ushakov adds in comments to Russian state TV. "Both during the plenary session of the Apec summit and immediately after it concludes."
"The leaders will meet, believe me, and they will have a substantive conversation, regardless of where they happen to be sitting - in armchairs, on chairs or on stools - or standing face-to-face, looking each other in the eye. The meeting will take place. Our president and the US president will meet a few times over the course of the summit," Ushakov says.
He also hints the meeting could take place on the sidelines of the summit, without the presence of large delegations.
The trilateral meeting between China, the US and Russia is reportedly set to take place at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen on Thursday, with security significantly tightened ahead of the talks.
The state-owned compound, which opened in 1997, has long hosted Chinese leaders and high-profile foreign visitors to the city.
Beijingâs decision to opt for a more private setting rather than a formal conference venue suggests the meeting is âmore of a sideline rather than a separate, significant summit on its ownâ, says Minseon Ku of DePaul University, a specialist in summit diplomacy.
âXi would want that, since, as the host of Apec, China would want the Apec summit to be the primary event and would not want the trilateral meeting to overshadow it,â she tells the BBC.
Professor Shaoyu Yuan of New York University, who studies US-China diplomacy, notes that Kylin Villa is relatively easy to secure. Its proximity to the airport would also allow Trump to depart directly after the meeting.
"The setting carries less diplomatic formality than an official venue in Beijing, framing the roughly one-hour meeting as a working-level engagement. The lower the ceremonial profile, the lower the political cost if the meeting produces no tangible outcomes," he says.
Laura Bicker China correspondent
Jens

articles.title_orig: Trump and Xi hug on tarmac as Trump arrives in China
articles.title_zh: Trump and Xi hug on tarmac as Trump arrives in China
articles.content_orig:
SHENZHEN, China — Chinese President Xi Jinping made a surprise appearance to greet President Trump on the tarmac Wednesday as he arrived in China — with the men shaking hands and hugging ahead of a historic trilateral summit Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Xi rarely greets visiting foreign leaders when they land, dispatching the fifth-ranking Communist Party official to meet Putin earlier Wednesday at Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport and sending his vice president to welcome Trump to Beijing in May.
The Chinese president’s unusual gesture of respect reciprocated Trump’s greeting of Xi at Joint Base Andrews outside Washington in September. Trump’s in-person welcome was the first for the visiting foreign leader since 1962.
Trump arrived in the Chinese boomtown just north of Hong Kong for the annual APEC conference following a stop in the Philippines.
Hundreds of performers waving flowers lined the red carpet in Shenzhen, chanting “enthusiastic warm welcome” in Mandarin — with the pageantry also featuring a military flyover, which Trump applauded.
The tributes to Trump continued into the evening, with classical musicians performing “America the Beautiful” as he arrived for a banquet featuring leaders of the 21 Pacific Rim economies comprising APEC.
Xi seated Trump next to him at the dinner’s head table and used an opening speech to the group to call for maintaining “the Asia-Pacific miracle of rapid economic growth.”
Putin approached Trump for a handshake ahead of the meal.
The highly anticipated trilateral meeting on Thursday — the first ever between the leaders of China, Russia and the US — will focus on nuclear disarmament.
The summit also will feature discussion of how the powers can work together to resolve the US war with Iran and end the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Trump said as he departed Washington.
Trump said he may also raise the scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy seducing the ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , who joined Trump on his trip to Beijing earlier this year — though the president expressed concern about insulting China by pressing the matter.
The summit will follow a bilateral meeting on Thursday between Trump and Xi that’s expected to address continuing trade tensions after last year’s tariff war.
US officials said prior to the trip that China continues to throttle its exports of rare earth minerals and magnets — leaving uncertain the fate of a trade truce reached last October.
Elon Musk, the CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, will participate in some events during the whirlwind visit to Shenzhen — though what exactly his role will be remains murky.
Trump has emphasized his interest in maintaining warm personal relations with both Xi and Putin as a way to advance US interests and resolve world issues.
Since his first term, he has pined for a pact between the world’s three most powerful nuclear-armed states, and the meeting is expected to be a preliminary step toward reducing stockpiles.
Trump has teased further surprises on the trip — suggesting that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un may also appear for what would be their first meeting since Trump returned to power last year.

articles.title_orig: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.title_zh: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is a cultural and economic earthquake. Brace yourself.
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, against the backdrop of the Miami-inspired Vice City. Rockstar Games hide caption
I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill from In The Air Tonight played on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI , probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
Lucia begins her epic as a petty criminal. Rockstar Games hide caption
The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
Help me, Lucia , she says.
And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this is also a story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
It's a story about my mom and an alligator, sure.
It is also the story of GTA6
Grand Theft Auto VI returns to Vice City and its Florida-inspired environs. Rockstar Games hide caption
But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years, Grand Theft Auto VI is the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release of GTA: Vice City , and is the first new game in the franchise since GTA5 launched in 2013. According to estimates, it already earned over $1.5 billion in pre-sales and will likely make a total of $3 to $5 billion in its first week , which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
Fans have been waiting years for it. They have created libraries worth of lore and theories and dissected trailers frame-by-frame. To discount the overheated environment into which this singular work of art is being released would be doing a disservice both to it and the legions of salivating prognosticators who have made guessing the number of bird species included in-game , or speculating on the square mileage of its map, their entire personalities.
While Vice City remains the game's hub, most of its map is actually rural or wild. Rockstar Games hide caption
Now, though, they know it all. We all do. We know that GTA6 is expansive, covering everything from the Keys (where the game starts) to the hilly, forested north, with Vice City in all its grimy, pastel-colored splendor at the beating heart of it. It is a playground, equal parts gorgeous and maniacal, and in all that space the developers have given us a thousand different things to do. You can rob a bank or take a bike ride, go fishing, hunt trophy animals, visit strip clubs, rob random civilians, street race, fly drones, eat a sandwich, work out, manage your family savings account, jump a sports car off the top of a building, steal a plane, punch out a convenience store clerk, fight a bear or, yes, just wander out toward the horizon and study the birds. And while some of that is fun and all of it is diverting (at least for a little while), none of it is the ostensible point. The game-y part of the game — the hundred extras and time-wasters that players have come to expect from open-world projects in general, and GTA specifically — is not what makes it matter.
What matters is Mia and the alligator, Lucia and the gun. It's the multi-pronged, exquisitely balanced narrative about poverty and rigged systems that makes it hard to turn away from GTA while you're playing and impossible not to think about when you're away.
Jason and his pal, Cal, shoot pool. Rockstar Games hide caption
Lucia is an ex-con, a car thief and a small-time criminal who got caught trying to rob a payday loan joint and starts the game in jail. Her partner, Jason Duval, is a veteran, dishonorably discharged, now making a living flying loads for a local coke dealer down in the Keys and living rent-free in one of his properties. Jason skims a little on the coke deals, wears flip-flops and drinks beer in the sun, and goes fishing with his best friend Cal (played with genius-level goofy, drunken paranoia and dopey bravado by Bobby Moynihan). Jason and Lucia have a kid, Tomás, who is currently living with Lucia's family, and every plan they have is about getting right by the law, making a few bucks and grabbing a chance at finally being a family.
Only there are complications — surprisingly banal ones at first (like not being able to open a checking account because of their bad credit) — that slowly ramp up into huge ones across 60-odd hours of main story gameplay that see Jason and Lucia (both of whom are playable characters) graduate from knocking over liquor stores in a beat-up El Camino, to pulling off elaborate heists in the middle of Vice City which will have you dangling from a net suspended from a cargo helicopter hauling 200 tons of cocaine. It goes from Badlands to Die Hard with the speed of a muscle car, all bright chrome and barking straight pipes. From True Romance to Heat like that's just the natural arc of any American love story.
And what's remarkable about the whole bloody delight is that it remains, until its final operatic moments, so surprisingly grounded. This is a somewhat more mature GTA than its predecessors, trading aliens, cannibal cultists and whacked-out drug trips for wellness influencers, local politics and the music industry. Jason and Lucia's relationship is the superstructure around which the entire narrative is built, and it's a dynamic thing that must be maintained in a dozen little ways — making coffee in the morning, opening doors for each other, date nights (even if that means robbing a jewelry store together), or holding hands as you walk toward yet another betrayal by someone you thought you could trust. articles.title_orig: Trump seeks to show strength in China, but a series of technological snafus raises concerns at home
articles.title_zh: Trump seeks to show strength in China, but a series of technological snafus raises concerns at home
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump greets as China's President Xi Jinping welcomes him after Trump steps off Air Force One at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen in southern China's Guangdong Province, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Mark Schiefelbein/AP hide caption
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday, seeking to reinforce the U.S. status as the world's leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left the administration scrambling to calm the American public.
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty ahead of a potentially complicated trilateral meeting on Thursday with the presidents of China and Russia, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the United States worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
"It's fine," Trump pronounced on Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is "big and powerful."
But then the outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency's communications network began to overshadow Trump's visit. They raised the specter that artificial intelligence can disrupt daily life, as new cyber vulnerabilities identified require software to be constantly upgraded to fix flaws or other security holes, known as patching, which is supposed to improve how the technology runs.
So at the start of the second day of Trump's trip, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stepped in to reassure Americans on Trump's behalf. He told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages are connected or tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.
"Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption," said Rubio, who is also Trump's national security adviser.
Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, China, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
The two leaders greeted each other at the foot of the airplane's stairs in a handshake that became a hug as group of dancers waved flowers and flags. When Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their longstanding friendship.
Trump has signaled that he wants to take an improvised approach during his time in Shenzhen, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House.
On Thursday, at a first-ever trilateral, Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.
Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be on the agenda. But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.
"I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that."
Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was "serious" about meeting with Kim as a way of resolving tensions with North Korea. But he suggested no meeting was currently scheduled between Trump and Kim for Thursday.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, walks beside U.S. President Donald Trump during a welcome ceremony marking Trump's state visit to the Philippines at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Aaron Favila/AP hide caption
Before he landed in Shenzhen, Trump had lunch in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the Malacañang Presidential Palace.
Marcos noted that he had sent fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee to the U.S. delegation for a late-night snack Tuesday and complimented Trump for "working very hard."
Trump praised the U.S. bond with the Philippines and the interior decoration of the presidential palace.
"Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes," Trump said. "I love what you've done here."
He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached. The U.S. trade deficit in goods with the Philippines has risen under Trump, climbing from $4.9 billion in 2024 to $12.8 billion during the first 9 months of this year, according to the Census Bureau.
There were no details about the new agreement, although the White House said it will involve Manila buying more energy and farm products.
Trump also had a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady and mother of the Philippines' current president.
Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader.
Trump called her "always the most beautiful" and the 97-year-old matriarch appeared to hand him a gift, according to a video posted by the White House.
Russian President Vladimir Putin speaks at the APEC CEO summit held ahead of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, southern China's Guangdong province on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. Dmitry Azarov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
The prospect of Trump meeting with two of America's largest geopolitical rivals has been a source of unease as the U.S. president has been less welcoming of historic allies such as Canada and NATO partners in Europe.
His tariffs that were intended to curb China's trade surplus have done little to stop the progress of the world's dominant manufacturer, which for the second straight year will have exported $1 trillion more in goods than what it imported.
Even without the digital outages in the U.S., questions about how to handle AI loom over the summit.
The technology is viewed as key to unlocking faster economic growth, but its rapid development has meant it poses national security risks and could evolve in ways that put AI beyond human control.
Trump's close tech industry ally Jensen Huang was recently removed as the CEO of Nvidia after he admitted to an affair with a woman alleged to be an agent of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied that she was a spy, yet the affair raised concerns about how China has been able to access Nvidia computer chips to develop its own AI models that are competing with the U.S.
When asked this week why the U.S. had not been more aggressive in cutting off China's access to advanced computer chips, Trump said there were differences of opinion inside his administration and that "We have a very good relationship with China, and you don't want to insult them."
Trump has said he does not plan to bring up Taiwan, a self-governing island that China claims as its own. Taiwan is the leading manufacturer of advanced computer chips, including those designed by U.S. companies.
Still, Trump expects that Xi will push him on Taiwan's sovereignty.
"I'm sure he'll raise it," Trump said. "I won't have to raise it."

articles.title_orig: The Bank of Nvidia's tab jumped to nearly $670 billion — and its customers are taking longer to pay: Chart of the Day
articles.title_zh: The Bank of Nvidia's tab jumped to nearly $670 billion — and its customers are taking longer to pay: Chart of the Day
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Jensen Huang started reining in the Bank of Nvidia months before he left. It got bigger anyway.
Third quarter results from Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Tuesday covered the last quarter during which Huang served as CEO. They also updated the number investors have watched since his exit put the company's web of AI deals under the microscope.
Everything Nvidia has promised to buy, back, or invest now comes to nearly $670 billion, up from about $530 billion in July, by Yahoo Finance calculations.
Most of the jump is for chips, not loans. Promises to suppliers swelled to $390 billion from $279 billion, mostly to lock up memory for years to come.
The riskier piece is the backstops. Nvidia carries $118 billion in guarantees — promises to pay if a partner can't — including nearly $10 billion in new ones for partners it didn't name. It says it hasn't paid out on any of them.
"Neoclouds and frontier labs are seeing extraordinary demand for AI infrastructure, yet many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support," interim CEO Colette Kress wrote in her commentary on the quarter .
New pledges did shrink, to $32 billion for neoclouds — cloud companies that rent out Nvidia's chips — and $20 billion for investments in other companies.
But the checks kept coming. Nvidia bought nearly $16 billion of stakes in other companies in the quarter, mostly private ones it didn't name. Among public companies, its latest holdings filing shows it added to SpaceX ( SPCX ) while trimming Intel ( INTC ) and Nokia ( NOK ). So far this fiscal year, those purchases have eaten up nearly half of the cash its business generated, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
Nvidia's accounts receivable — bills sent but not yet paid — hit $81 billion, or 64 days of sales. That's the most since the 2022 chip slump by a measure called days sales outstanding .
Nvidia pointed to "extended payment terms on large, multi-quarter agreements with certain investment-grade customers." In other words, some of its biggest buyers are getting more time to pay.
The full books will have to wait. Nvidia said its 10-Q quarterly report would come "in the coming weeks," not the same evening as usual. Its release also mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.
"The deep financing arm of Nvidia is ... a moat that no competitor is ... going to be able to get close to anytime soon," Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy, told Yahoo Finance last week.
Skeptics point to the pandemic-era chip shortage, in which long-term deals didn't protect suppliers once demand slowed. "And then all these long-term supply agreements basically are worthless, right?" Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management told Yahoo Finance Tuesday.
On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled the bank may be choosier from here. "As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees," she said.
Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.
Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

articles.title_orig: GTA 6 about to launch in UK after 13-year wait and two delays
articles.title_zh: GTA 6 about to launch in UK after 13-year wait and two delays
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has begun its launch, ending gamers' 13-year wait for a new instalment
The game launches at midnight around the world, meaning gamers in New Zealand became the first to play at 11:00 GMT
Initial reviews give the game a score of 99 , according to Metacritic
The crime game , where players can explore a fictional US state called Leonida, features the series' first playable female protagonist in a 3D setting
Analysts believe the game cost more than $1bn (Â£866m) to develop - in the UK, it is priced at Â£69.99 and in the US at $79.99
The game was delayed twice, from autumn 2025, and then May 2026, before finally launching
Edited by Tinshui Yeung and Joe Coughlan
More than 2.4 million people are currently watching gamers play GTA 6 on Twitch, a website where people can watch and comment on others playing video games.
Content creators are trying a variety of ways to attract viewers, including saying theyâll be the first to complete the game, playing it with their partners and giving away merchandise.
For comparison, the second most popular category on Twitch is creators talking without playing a video game, with 136,000 viewers. The third most popular is World of Warcraft, with about 76,000 viewers.
While gamers in New Zealand have started playing GTA 6, many of you in the UK are waiting patiently for it to drop here later tonight.
Gaming livestreamer Alana Black, who you might know better as Alana CJ on Twitch, says she'll spend the day doing her best to avoid spoilers.
"I just try to swipe past it, ignore it and don't peek at it,â she says.
And her advice if you're trying to do the same? "Lock your phone away, turn off all devices, don't go near any social media.â
The 30-year-old tells BBC Newsbeat she knows gamers who might be trying to use what's called the "New Zealand trick" to access the game early by changing their console's location.
"You can be banned for it,â she warns.
âI wouldn't risk it personally. It's been 13 years since the last GTA, I can wait one more day."
As weâve just reported, reviews on Metacritic have given the game an average score of 99 .
The New York Times , external has called the instalment a "dense game filled with friction", saying it "matures beyond its memorable car crashes and stick-ups with a game about love, relationships and nurturing your partner".
Gaming website IGN , external has given the game a score of 10 out of 10, describing it as "exquisitely detailed" and "uncompromisingly engineered".
The lowest confirmed reviews on the website currently give the game a score of 90.
Entertainment outlet Slant Magazine , external says there are "flaws" in the game's creative approach in its four-and-a-half-star review, with its fantasy taking "power away from the player" at regular checkpoints.
Laura Cress Technology reporter
When Victoria Evans filed a leave request at work, the reason she gave was âGTA 6â. She told the BBC her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".
Anyway, the request was approved, and Victoria will get up at 05:00 GMT on Thursday to play, after its launch at midnight in the UK.
Sheâs far from the only one. For the gameâs launch day, HR software company BrightHR looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees at 70,000 businesses across the UK.
It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of employeesâ time-off requests.
It said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game throughout November and December.
Booking leave is only one way fans are making sure theyâre ready for the big day.
Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending theyâre halfway around the world to get early access.
Tom Gerken Technology reporter
The reviews are in, and it appears the hype was for good reason.
GTA 6 has an average review score of 99 on Metacritic , external , based on 100 critic reviews.
That means itâs - at least for now - tied for the top spot with the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which also scored 99 when it launched on the N64 in 1998.
Not all the reviews may be in yet, so the final score could be a bit different.
Some sites may want to experience more of the game before finalising their scores.
But whatever the case, with countless reviewers giving GTA 6 perfect marks, this is a remarkable case of a game delivering on its truly monstrous hype.
GTA 6âs predecessor was a record-breaker, and this new title is widely expected to be the biggest entertainment release ever.
GTA 5 made Rockstar $1bn (Â£760m) in just three days after its release. Unsurprisingly, it holds the record for the best opening-week sales in video game history.
The figure is on a par with the cost of developing GTA 6: estimates also put the cost of creating the game at about $1bn.
Tom Gerken Technology reporter
Sometimes, studios release games worldwide all at once.
Other times, perhaps to reduce the burden on servers, they stagger the release - launching a game at midnight across different time zones. GTA 6 falls into the latter category.
As the Earth continues to rotate on its axis, more and more people will start playing GTA 6.
The latest game in the Grand Theft Auto franchise has now released in New Zealand at midnight local time (11:00 GMT).
Gamers who have pre-installed the game should now be able to launch it on their consoles.
Weâll bring you the first reactions shortly.
Laura Cress and Liv McMahon Technology reporters
GTA 6 features the first ever playable female protagonist in a 3D and HD setting for the series - Lucia - alongside her partner in life and crime, Jason, as a second playable character.
From what we've seen in two gameplay trailers and Netflix's extended look, the story will follow the pair in a Bonnie and Clyde-esque adventure through the seedy underbelly of America after an "easy score goes wrong".
Like other GTA games before it, the sixth chapter is set in a fictional US state - this time in Leonida, which is Rockstar's version of Florida.
Fans of previous games will be excited to hear that Vice City, which is inspired by Miami, will return, featuring as the main city within the state.
GTA 6's cover art, revealed by Rockstar on 18 June, made several nods to the setting with alligators and flamingos.
Laura Cress and Liv McMahon Technology reporters
The sixth game in the main series is being released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S.
Thereâs no news on when a PC version will be released. Itâs also currently unknown whether itâll come to Nintendo Switch 2.
The game is priced at Â£69.99 in the UK and $79.99 in the US. An ultimate edition, featuring extra vehicles and weapons, is priced at Â£89.99 and $99.99 respectively.
Physical copies of the game contain a code for a digital download inside the box, rather than a disc.
Tom Gerken Technology reporter
After 13 years of speculation, rumour and hype, weâre minutes away from the launch of one of the most anticipated games ever.
Thatâs a long time for any series, let alone one of the five best-selling gaming franchises in history.
There are suggestions anticipation has reached such a fever pitch that thousands have booked leave just to play the game, while others might be thinking of calling in sick.
In the game, players control criminals as they navigate fictional cities, steal cars and complete missions. Itâs become a behemoth.
Fans are waiting with bated breath to finally play the game theyâve waited more than a decade for.
Rockstar Games is releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 to gamers around the world at midnight on Thursday, 19 November. Players in New Zealand will be among the first to experience the game, at 11:00 GMT.
The game's release follows two delays, after it was initially due to launch in autumn 2025.
The previous instalment in the series, GTA 5, sold around 235 million copies and is one of the best-selling video games of all time.
We'll bring you all the latest updates on the game's release here.
Buckle in. Next stop, Vice City.

articles.title_orig: Stock futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures rise as Nvidia gains on earnings beat and solid outlook: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
Stock futures climbed Wednesday morning after the S&P 500 fell for a fourth straight day. Traders also weighed Nvidia 's better-than-expected earnings report.
Nasdaq-100 futures were up 1%, while S&P 500 futures added 0.58%. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up 0.32%.
Shares of Nvidia were almost 3% higher in premarket trade, after jumping 4% in extended trading after the company's profit and revenue in the third quarter beat analysts' estimates. The company also lifted its revenue guidance for the fiscal year ending January 2028, calling for 75% growth year over year.
"The fact that they gave guidance is huge," said Gene Munster, managing partner at Deepwater Asset Management, on CNBC's "Closing Bell: Overtime. " " That is a very bullish sign. I expect the stock to move higher based just on that alone."
Neocloud companies also rose in extended trading. CoreWeave advanced 8%, while Nebius Group gained 10%.
During the regular trading day, the Dow dropped 1.6%. The S&P 500 slipped 1% and notched its lowest closing level since July 29, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 0.7%. During the day, the tech-heavy index touched its lowest level since April.
Looking ahead, traders are awaiting building permits and housing starts data. The Federal Open Market Committee's minutes from its October meeting will also be out in the afternoon. Federal Reserve policymakers last month decided to keep the overnight funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%.
On the earnings front, Lowe's, Target and TJ Maxx-parent TJX Cos are slated to report Wednesday morning.
Later this week, investors are awaiting a blockbuster initial public offering from Anthropic. The AI giant's shares are expected to be priced above the current range between $70 and $78, multiple sources told CNBC's David Faber on Tuesday.
Across the Atlantic, stock markets were mixed on Wednesday, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 hovering just below the flatline in morning trade. The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was 0.34% down, with France's CAC 40 sliding almost 0.1%, but Germany's DAX advanced 0.15%.
Most Asian markets closed in positive territory after a choppy trading session. South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights gained ground, ending 1.99% higher at 5,067.44, while Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28,
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was 0.87% lower in its final hour of trade, while the CSI 300 on mainland China advanced 0.18% to 3,983.77. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.69%, marking a fifth straight day of losses.
Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at New Jersey-based Questar Capital Partners, said in a note Wednesday that Nvidia is "uninvestable."
"Nvidia is the Jenga tower of the whole AI trade, and that is not a compliment," he said. "A week ago, we thought this was a pedestrian story about a CEO whose ego got the best of him. Then we found out there was no clear succession plan, and poor corporate governance, with no Chairman until this scandal came to light."
He added that Nvidia's delayed 10-Q was a "red flag, as it's out of character from its previous releases."
"We believe there are significant questions about where Nvidia has been selling its chips," Reyle said. "For investors who own the stock, this is an immediate sell in our view. We have never owned Nvidia and believe the stock has been and remains uninvestable."
Shares of Nvidia were up around 4% in pre-market trading on Wednesday.
"There's another company set to begin a spectacular run (Anthropic), and every moment spent worrying about Nvidia is time that could have been spent finding the next winner," Reyle added. "News flash: NVDA ain't it."
Nvidia stock was up nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday after reporting another earnings beat , as the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's resignation continues to unfold.
The chip giant's stock was 3.96% higher at 5.08 a.m. ET on Wednesday in pre-market trading.
Neoclouds were buoyed by the results. CoreWeave was up 6.2%, Nebius 8.1% and Iren 7.4%.
U.S.-listed semiconductor stocks rose in pre-market trading Wednesday, following Nvidia's earnings beat.
Ahead of the opening bell, Nvidia stock was trading 3.9% higher, with the iShares and VanEck semiconductor ETFs both adding around 2.8%.
Marvell Technology added 4.3%, Arm was up by 3.8% and Micron gained 3.6%. KLA Corporation and AMD also traded more than 3% higher.
President Donald Trump has landed in China for the APEC summit, where he is due to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the first trilateral talks between the three leaders on Thursday.
The meeting — taking place in Shenzhen, a major tech hub — puts trade and technology in sharp focus. Markets will be watching for any sign of progress on U.S.-China trade tensions or restrictions on advanced AI chips.
Xi opened the summit by calling for fewer trade and investment barriers and closer cooperation on artificial intelligence.
Traders are also watching for any signal on Ukraine, sanctions and energy, and the conflict in the Middle East , which could shape expectations for Russian oil exports and the geopolitical risk premium.
Precious metals sold off Wednesday morning, with gold falling to its lowest level in over a year and silver also plunging to a 52-week low, as expectations of interest rate rises from the Federal Reserve next month drew investors away from non-interest bearing assets.
Gold futures fell 2.34% to $3,761.84, while spot gold was down 2.38% at $3,758%. Silver futures slipped 3.5% to $45.72, as spot silver shed 3.6% to reach $45.67.
Nannette Hechler-Fayd'herbe, Lombard Odier Group's chief investment officer for EMEA and head of investment strategy, sustainability and research, said she remained optimistic on gold over the next 12 months, but warned that investors may need to be patient.
Hechler-Fayd'herbe does not expect the Federal Reserve or other central banks to embark on a sustained series of interest-rate hikes. But with U.S. real yields moving back up to 2.9%, from 2.6% not long ago, conditions are not yet supportive of an immediate rally, she said.
"This of course is not an environment where gold can immediately perform, so a little bit of patience on gold I think is warranted," she told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday.
European stock markets were largely negative in early trading on Wednesday, with the Stoxx 600 edging just below the flatline shortly after 8:00 a.m. in London (3:00 a.m. E.T.).
Technology stocks advanced 1.16%, leading continental sectors, while industrial goods added 0.19%. But most other sectors were in the red, with basic resources tumbling 2.41%, while autos fell 0.43%.
Germany's DAX was up almost 0.1% in early trading in Frankfurt.
The U.K.'s FTSE 100 was down 0.32% in London, while in Paris, the CAC 40 was flat.  In Milan, the Italian FTSE MIB was hovering just below the flatline.
Indonesia's central bank on Wednesday raised rates by 25 basis points in a surprise move, bringing its policy rate to 6% — last seen in December 2024.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected the bank to keep rates steady at 5.75%.
The Bank of Indonesia said the move was to strengthen the currency and a preemptive measure to keep inflation in its target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
The Indonesian rupiah depreciated to a record low of 18,285 against the greenback on Tuesday, while the inflation rate in the country was at 3.23% in October.
Markets in Asia ended mostly higher on Wednesday in choppy trading as investors assessed Nvidia earnings, Japan exports data, and comments from global leaders at the APEC summit in China.
South Korea's Kospi led gains in the region as chip heavyweights rose, rising 2% to 5,067.44. The small-cap Kosdaq also advanced 2% to close at 662.81.
Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 0.28% to close at 59,024.28, while the broad-broad Topix lost 0.42% to 3,824.

articles.title_orig: Trump begins China visit marked by high-stakes talks on war and trade
articles.title_zh: Trump begins China visit marked by high-stakes talks on war and trade
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred
GUANGZHOU, China — Behind the scenes, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spent months pushing for action that would signal resolve within the Trump administration against China’s pursuit of the most powerful American computer chips, a flashpoint  in their race for superiority in artificial intelligence, multiple sources said.
But President Trump’s courtship of Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, seeking to alleviate tensions between the world’s greatest powers, and a contingent of advisors skeptical of commercial warfare against Beijing slowed the process down — giving China months of opportunity to gain access to U.S. semiconductors through the back door.
Ultimately, just hours before departing for Asia alongside  Trump, Bessent got his way, bolstering his position ahead of talks with Chinese officials in Shenzhen this week on the risks posed by frontier systems.
A new rule tightening loopholes in U.S. export controls sends a dual message to Beijing ahead of Thursday’s summit: that Washington is serious about curbing Chinese circumvention — and that China hawks within the administration may be gaining the upper hand.
Trump has repeatedly sidestepped confrontation with Xi over the intensifying AI race in their two previous meetings this year, in Beijing and Washington, wary of upsetting a carefully managed detente and reluctant to jeopardize a technology boom increasingly central to the U.S. economy.
The new rules restrict remote access to advanced U.S. computing chips and servers, marking the latest step to limit China’s abilities to use U.S. chips to train their best AI models.
But the administration, from the president down, is acutely aware of China’s ambitions to dominate an industry that could reshape the global balance of power. That competitive drive was underscored this month by a scandal involving a Chinese espionage campaign targeting Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, the world’s leading AI chip maker.
Before resigning from the company in disgrace Thursday, Huang admitted to having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy — a woman who worked at a firm in Singapore accused by American authorities of helping to divert restricted Nvidia chips to China, in violation of U.S. export controls.
The national security scandal has roiled the markets — and in so doing, commanded Trump’s attention — inflicting a significant devaluation on Nvidia and reverberating well beyond it, wiping nearly $1 trillion from the combined market value of major technology companies in a single trading session on Monday.
Trump, who counts Huang a friend and ally, indicated he would be open to his return as Nvidia’s chief executive. Bessent suggested otherwise, expressing confidence its board could find competent new leadership and urging a full investigation.
Huang indicated his interest Tuesday in returning to Nvidia, writing in a social media post that “I would be honored” to resume his role as CEO if asked by the board of directors. But Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones said later Tuesday that the company does not intend to bring Huang back.
Trump is not expected to raise the Nvidia matter directly with Xi. But Bessent plans to do so in his own meetings, one official said.
The Treasury secretary has thus taken on the role of an enforcer, pursuing a tougher line than Trump is willing to take himself in his highly personalized relationship with the Chinese leader.
Bessent is scheduled to meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on the sidelines of the summitry in Shenzhen to discuss potential collaboration on AI safety protocols, standards for testing of advanced models, and a direct communications channel for AI emergencies.
The two men have met before to discuss AI, most recently in New York, where they agreed in principle to coordinate. But the talks have yet to produce much in the way of tangible results.
“Bessent is signaling that, while he sees working with Beijing to mitigate AI risks as a priority, it won’t come at the expense of actions that he sees as necessary to protect U.S. national security, like limiting AI chip exports to China,” said Daniel Remler, a senior fellow with the Technology and National Security Program at the Center for a New American Security.
The administration’s latest action marks a policy defeat for Howard Lutnick , secretary of the Commerce Department, who oversees chip policy and had advocated for a less restrictive approach than Bessent, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative.
The feud began spilling into public view ahead of the president’s travel, and in light of the Nvidia scandal, after Bessent said in a television interview that the Commerce Department “has the pen” to act, implying a split within the team.
“Look, there’re two different views,” Trump told reporters Monday, answering questions on the matter. “One view is you don’t want to insult China. We have a very good relationship with China, and you don’t want to insult them.”
“The other view is just go, you know, down and dirty and do what you have to do,” Trump continued. “You can’t say either is wrong or right. We’ll let you know.”
Beyond the diplomatic niceties, Trump has been explicit and consistent since resuming office that the United States must “win” the race for AI superiority, calling the alternative “not acceptable.”
“Whoever wins AI,” Trump said at the United Nations General Assembly in September, “whoever wins superintelligence, wins.”
Trump will arrive in China on Wednesday after meeting with world leaders in Manila, including those from the Quad — an alliance of Japan, India, Australia and the United States —  who discussed AI at their own summit Tuesday evening.
Describing “superintelligence” — Trump’s preferred term for AI — as “the greatest opportunity for economic growth since the Industrial Revolution,” Trump announced a Quad effort to accelerate adoption of the technology, including an investment of more than $85 million to enhance AI ecosystems throughout the region.
“We want to be careful with it,” Trump said, “but it’s amazing, the things that have come out, in terms of science and in terms of medical breakthroughs. No one can believe what we’re finding. And we’re finding it fast.”
“We want to be very careful, but we want to cherish it,” he added. “The United States as you know is leading in that capacity, by quite a bit.”
As he meets with the leaders of India, Japan and Australia, Trump will face pressure to sustain resolve against Beijing despite his yearlong courtship of President Xi Jinping.
The new U.S. rule requires overseas data centers serving customers in China, Russia, Iran and Cuba to identify their end users before gaining access to chips. It also imposes additional licensing requirements on chip sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which the Commerce Department identifies as posing a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” to unauthorized destinations.
U.S. officials say that export controls are not up for negotiation in talks with the Chinese. But Beijing sees them as yet another historic example of Washington trying to contain its rise — a posture that has repeatedly stifled diplomatic progress between the two superpowers.
“While administration officials say export controls aren’t up for negotiation, Chinese officials will certainly bring them up,” Remler said. “These restrictions are the key obstacle to China’s AI progress, which is increasingly important to the Chinese economy and to Xi’s strategic goals.”
China claims it does not seek an all-powerful, generalized “superintelligence,” but rather specialized AI systems embedded across industries to boost productivity and improve quality of life.

articles.title_orig: Trump heads to China after announcing 'very big trade deal' in Manila
articles.title_zh: Trump heads to China after announcing 'very big trade deal' in Manila
articles.content_orig:
President Trump said on Wednesday the United States had concluded a “very big trade deal” with the Philippines, but offered no details, while Manila said the two countries had reached only an understanding on economic cooperation.
“We’ve just consummated a very big trade deal, the biggest trade deal we’ve ever made so far, and it is a fair deal for both countries,” Trump told a state lunch event at the Philippine presidential palace.
“We were very happy with that, and we didn’t know that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly and it’s a magnificent deal for both.”
The Philippine president’s office later said both sides reached an understanding on areas of economic cooperation, but made no mention of a trade deal.
Trade representatives of both countries will work closely to translate the commitments into concrete initiatives, it said in a statement.
The deal with the Philippines would be great for US farmers and those in the energy business, Trump added on Truth Social, but gave no further details.
Negotiations on a trade deal between the two allies were not mentioned in any schedules released by either country.
There was no immediate comment from the office of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr about the deal Trump was referring to.
“The US offered for us to diversify our food supply and energy requirements,” said Jose Manuel Romualdez, the Philippines’ ambassador to the United States.
Asked whether anything was signed, Romualdez said in a text message, “None.”
On Tuesday, Trump said Thailand would scrap all tariffs and substantial non-tariff barriers on its imports from the United States in a trade deal expected to be finalized in coming weeks.

articles.title_orig: Xi Jinping greets Donald Trump with hug ahead of historic trilateral summit
articles.title_zh: Xi Jinping greets Donald Trump with hug ahead of historic trilateral summit
articles.content_orig:
• Trump welcomed in China: Chinese leader Xi Jinping broke precedent to greet US President Donald Trump in person at the airport in tech hub Shenzhen ahead of their meeting at the APEC summit. Trump arrived from the Philippines, where he held talks with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and other world leaders.
• Historic meeting: Trump will tomorrow hold unprecedented joint talks with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin , who said he expects “considerable potential benefits” from the talks. The US president does not view a potential sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un as a concession, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said.
• Xi slams “protectionism”: Earlier at the summit, Xi pitched China as a defender of the globalized economy and met with Putin, with the authoritarian leaders lauding their close ties .
US President Donald Trump will meet on Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China, during unprecedented trilateral talks together with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
But that is not the only occasion Trump and Putin will cross paths in the city.
The Russian leader spoke briefly with Trump at a gala reception for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit guests on Wednesday evening local time.
Kremlin foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Wednesday the pair could also meet tomorrow for separate talks.
Their meeting will be an “intimate affair” without the involvement of large delegations, Vesti cited Ushakov as saying.
Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said there is unlikely to be an opportunity for “full-format talks” between the US and Russian leaders, Russian state media TASS said.
He did however say the pair will likely discuss the Ukraine conflict and possibly Iran, TASS reported.
US President Donald Trump is now in Shenzhen, China, where he was greeted at the airport by Chinese leader Xi Jinping, a first for Xi in his current role.
Historically, it is extremely rare for China’s top leader to personally welcome foreign leaders upon their arrivals.
Trump is expected to take part in an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) banquet this evening, then several significant meetings tomorrow.
CNN’s Sylvie Zhuang, Kathleen Magramo and Lex Harvey contributed to this reporting.
For Xi Jinping, a summit in the high-tech hub of Shenzhen this week is an opportune moment to showcase a vision of China’s unrelenting rise.
Xi is hosting business moguls and world leaders for an annual regional economic summit, where he’ll sit down to sideline talks with US President Donald Trump and hold a three-way meeting with Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, a first-ever trilateral for the nuclear-armed powers.
And for his backdrop, Xi has chosen a host city that’s synonymous with China’s rapid transformation into a high-tech powerhouse — and its resilience in the face of US tech and trade frictions.
A sprawling metropolis of 18 million, Shenzhen is home to a who’s-who of Chinese tech titans: hardware giant Huawei, dronemaker DJI and the Tesla-beating electric vehicle seller BYD — all companies that have thrived despite US import bans or blacklists.
Once known as the capital of luxury knockoffs and cheap electronics, today the city’s high-tech products have helped propel China’s export juggernaut to a record $1 trillion trade surplus already this year.
Visiting VIPs who step out onto Shenzhen’s streets this week will find traffic that moves to the whir of homegrown electric vehicles and novelty kiosks where robots serve up coffee. Self-driving taxis ferry passengers and drones deliver take-out in some areas. Surveillance cameras are ubiquitous.
US President Donald Trump is now in Shenzhen, China, after spending part of the day in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, during his ongoing Asia tour.
Here’s a look at his remaining schedule:
Arriving in China for his second visit this year, Trump was greeted by enthusiastic spectators, a military flyover, an honor guard – and an embrace from Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
When Trump exited Air Force One, he was greeted by rows of young women and men wearing pink and baby blue who were holding flowers and shouting “Welcome!”
Xi and Trump embraced each other at the bottom of the steps. A girl handed Trump a bouquet of flowers, and then the US president shook hands with top communist party leaders one by one.
A People’s Liberation Army (PLA) honor guard was present and five military jets flew over the airport, leaving pink, blue and yellow smoke trails in the sky.
In a Xinhua readout of Xi’s remarks to Trump, the Chinese leader remembered how the US president and his wife made a “special trip to the airport to greet me, and a grand welcome ceremony was held,” referring to his trip to the US earlier this year.
“China is a nation of courtesy, with a tradition of reciprocity,” the readout quoted Xi as saying.
“I welcome you to visit China again, and I look forward to exchanging in-depth views with you on major issues concerning China-US. relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, so as to advance a constructive and stable strategic relationship between China and the United States based on respect, fairness, and reciprocity,” said Xi.
Last October, Chinese leader Xi Jinping sat down for a meeting with Japan’s newly elected prime minister Sanae Takaichi. The two countries should be “partners, not threats” to each other, Xi told her.
One year later, that hopeful statement has long been forgotten. China-Japan relations remain strained – with no sign the two leaders will meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit this week.
Their spat began just weeks after that first meeting when Takaichi suggested Japan could respond militarily if China were to move to take control of self-ruled Taiwan by force. China’s Communist Party claims Taiwan as its own territory, despite never having controlled it.
Taiwan is one of China’s red lines – and Beijing was furious that Takaichi crossed it. Since then, China has put economic pressure on Japan, warning its citizens not to travel there; nationalist and anti-Japanese fervor spread on Chinese social media; and dozens of Japanese performers canceled performances in China, even if they didn’t cite the diplomatic row as a reason.
When asked whether Xi would meet with Takaichi at APEC, a Chinese Foreign Affairs Ministry spokesperson gave a terse response.
That position is evident in a quick glance through the ministry’s briefings this past year.
The countries have a long history of animosity. In the early 20th century, Japan’s Imperial Army invaded China and committed war crimes – including the Nanjing massacre . Japan has repeatedly apologized for the atrocities, but they remain a sharp pain point.
During his time in the top job, Chinese leader Xi Jinping has never gone to the airport to receive a visiting US president.
In protocol-obsessed China, Xi’s presence on the red carpet in Shenzhen highlights the importance China attaches to its bilateral relationship with the US.
Earlier this year, Trump personally greeted Xi when he arrived by plane at Joint Base Andrews.
According to China’s diplomatic protocol in recent years, the head of state generally doesn’t go to the airport to greet guests.
When Russia’s President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen earlier today, he was met by Xi’s powerful chief of staff Cai Qi – itself an unusually high level of protocol.
Xi did greet then-US President Barack Obama at the airport in 2009, but he was China’s vice-president at the time.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping met with President Donald Trump at the airport in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday.
He awaited the US president at the bottom of the airplane steps.
President Donald Trump has been greeted by Chinese leader Xi Jinping after arriving in Shenzhen, China, ahead of their meeting at the APEC summit.
Xi’s presence on the red carpet at the airport mirrors Trump’s welcome of the Chinese leader when he visited the US this year.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.title_zh: Nvidia says no longer shipping 'Hopper' AI chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.
Nvidia messaged chip buyers in recent months to caution that the proposed Remote Access Security Act, or RASA, would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services in the same way as physical hardware, potentially exposing both parties to legal risk, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The people asked not to be named while discussing private communications.
It also said that, for now, it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, the people said.
Separately, the Financial Times reported earlier this month that Nvidia verbally told data-center clients to direct at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese customers under future contracts.
Regulators have had limited powers to control companies' access to those chips through cloud services hosted overseas.
RASA passed the House of Representatives in January but has not yet passed the Senate. Remote access to the chips has provoked the ire of President Donald Trump 's administration, which has sought to keep the chips out of China to maintain the U.S. lead in the AI race.
CNBC reported on Nov. 5 that Chinese lab Moonshot AI sought access to Nvidia chips through data centers in Europe. The Trump administration previously singled the company out, accusing it in July of accessing the chips through centers in East Asia.
The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, announced on Monday an interim final rule designed to prevent Chinese companies' remote access to AI chips.
Nvidia and BIS did not respond to a request for comment.
On Sunday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after Jensen Huang 's shock departure as CEO, amid reports of an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. authorities reportedly suspect of spying for China.
Bessent suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent told Fox News.
In an August securities filing , Nvidia said it sought to "strictly comply with all applicable export control regulators" but did not have "physical control of our products after sale" and relied on its customers' and partners' compliance programs.
Huang has been asked to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

Summit in Chinese tech hub Shenzhen set to include highly anticipated meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin
Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit
What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds
US president Donald Trump shakes hands with Russian president Vladimir Putin , as China’s Xi Jinping looks on, ahead of the welcome banquet at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China:
Donald Trump has arrived at the welcome banquet with Xi Jinping:
The newswires are carrying pictures of world leaders arriving for the welcome banquet at the Apec summit, including Russia’s Vladimir Putin:
Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump could have several opportunities to speak during the Apec summit in China, according to Russia’s state news agency, Tass.
Citing Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov , Tass reported that the two leaders could exchange words informally at various points during the summit.
They will communicate “on their feet, on the steps, in chairs”, Ushakov reportedly said, suggesting their interactions need not be limited to a formal sit-down meeting.
Xi Jinping told Donald Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity” , according to China’s state news agency Xinhua .
Xi also recalled Trump’s personal welcome at the airport during his visit to the US in September, saying China’s own welcome for the US president reflected its tradition of reciprocity.
Xinhua reported the following remarks by the Chinese president:
double quotation mark When I visited the United States in September this year, president Trump and his wife made a special trip to the airport to welcome me, and a grand welcoming ceremony was held.
China is a nation of courtesy, with a tradition of reciprocity. I welcome you back to China and look forward to exchanging in-depth views with you on major issues concerning China–US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape, so as to advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.”
Chinese state media have released a readout of Xi Jinping’s earlier meeting with Vladimir Putin .
In it, Xi is quoted as saying China-Russia relations are “unshaken by storms and steady as a mountain” , and have set “an example of a new type of major-country relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trustworthiness, and win-win co-operation”.
Xi also urged closer political and military ties between the two countries. He said “the two sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties, ensuring that the consensus reached by the two countries’ heads of state is effectively implemented”, according to the readout.
In a notable gesture, Xi personally greeted Trump on the airport tarmac in Shenzhen , reciprocating the welcome the US president extended to the Chinese leader during his visit to the US in September.
As a reminder, Ukraine carried out a major strike on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia, destroying its central road section in an operation involving two strikes over consecutive days.
The attack earlier this week dealt a significant blow to a key transport link and a symbolic project for Vladimir Putin , as the Russian president sat down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping for talks at the Apec summit.
My colleague Jakub Krupa has the latest on the Ukraine conflict over on our Europe live blog here:
While we await Trump to disembark Air Force Once, we have this report from our China correspondent Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen:
Canada’s Mark Carney has hit back at Vladimir Putin’s earlier assertion that sanctions no longer work in this day and age.
“Mr Putin can ask his financial institutions, he can ask his oligarch friends, he can ask his hockey players whether or not sanctions are a thing of the past. I think he’ll find out that they’re very real, they’re biting,” Carney told reporters.
In his address to the summit this morning, Putin had said that “the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having ⁠lost much of their intimidating power”.
Speaking at an outdoor press conference as purple clouds lingered ominously in the background, Carney said: “Not for the first time, Vladimir Putin is lying about the situation on the ground. Sanctions are very real and they’re going to continue to increase as long as this war goes on.”
Carney had previously said he would not boycott a group photo with Putin out of respect for hosts China . But he said if he were to find himself next to the Russian president, he would make Canada’s position clear.
Carney met China’s president Xi Jinping on Tuesday, with the two countries announcing remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
The two men also discussed AI, Carney said Wednesday, adding he had taken the opportunity to share Canada’s views on a model for global governance.
“The absence of any global governance around AI is an enormous risk,” he said. “It’s an enormous economic risk but it’s a biohazard risk, and it’s a risk to democracy, human dignity, other factors... So it is past time to develop global governance frameworks for these sectors.”
Carney is due to meet Donald Trump later today, he said, where they would discuss efforts to reach a trade deal.
“We have been making progress... Two steps forward, one step back type thing,” he said.
He said he fully respected Trump’s engagement with China.
“I’m going to say something positive here about the initiative around denuclearization, the trilateral meeting that is going to happen,” he said. “Guess what? Canada’s in favor of denuclearization. If the relationship can be used towards that end, we’re very much supportive of it.”
Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen, China, for the Apec summit, Chinese state media reported.
